subject: Lumos trial: workload intake + success criteria checklist
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Priya Sharma <priya@lumosanalytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-29T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Lumos trial: workload intake + success criteria checklist

Hi Priya — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and the next steps we discussed so the trial kickoff stays on schedule. I pasted the items we need from your side and assigned owners on our end.

Summary of what you told us on the call:
- Primary workload: customer support assistant that ingests chat and ticket history, returns short answer + citations, and occasionally reranks candidate passages.
- Typical prompt size: user message ~20–120 tokens; context/history average ~800 tokens (when included).
- Embeddings used for retrieval layer; generation endpoint used for final responses.
- Traffic shape: baseline ~180 RPS during business hours, expected peak bursts up to ~1,100 RPS for 45–90s during campaign spikes; concurrency target ~70 concurrent generation sessions.

What Redwood needs (action items for Lumos) — please share the files by EOD Thursday if possible:
1) Example request traces (anonymized): 48–72 hours of representative requests, with token counts and response size. File: lumos_token_profile.csv (see attachment stub).
2) A 1–2 sample prompt set that includes long-context cases (history + prompt) and short interactions. File: lumos_sample_requests.json.
3) Success criteria: define latency SLO, quality thresholds (e.g., precision@1 for reranker, acceptable hallucination rate), and cost targets for the pilot. We proposed below a baseline SLO of p95 generation latency < 350ms and rerank return < 200ms for sampled cases — confirm if that aligns.

Redwood owners & next steps:
- Marissa (me): overall trial timeline, kickoff, and mutual action plan (MAP).
- Ben Carter (cc): benchmark configuration and load orchestration owner — he will validate the RPS/concurrency windows.
- Soojin Lee (cc): evaluation QA — will own qualitative checks and regression testing.

Proposed timeline:
- Thu 2027-04-01: Receive request traces + prompt samples + success criteria (LumOS).
- Mon 2027-04-05: Redwood delivers preliminary capacity/instance recommendation and an initial MAP doc (mutual-action-plan-v1.pdf attached).
- Wed 2027-04-07: Small-scale smoke run with a subset of requests (sanity & latency).
- Tue 2027-04-13: Full trial window starts (7 days).

Questions for you (short):
- Any PII or regulated content in the examples we should know about (PII masking already suggested on our side)?
- Do you plan to use prefix caching or session affinity in your app logic? That affects cache-hit expectations.

If that all looks right, confirm and send the three artifacts. I’ll schedule Ben for a brief kickoff calibration call for load patterns.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Mid-Market AE | Redwood Inference
Attachment stubs: lumos_token_profile.csv (CSV, ~12 KB), lumos_sample_requests.json (JSON, ~18 KB)
From: Priya Sharma <priya@lumosanalytics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Amit Desai <amit@lumosanalytics.com>, procurement@lumosanalytics.com
Date: 2027-03-30T09:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Lumos trial: workload intake + success criteria checklist

Hi Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. We're aligned on most points. Attaching the requested sample files (see attachment stubs). A few clarifications:  

- The 1,100 RPS peak is the absolute max when a marketing campaign triggers; typical business-hours baseline is closer to 150–200 RPS sustained. Bursts last 45–90s and happen roughly 2–3x per weekday for the pilot segment.
- Token breakdown: median user prompt 45 tokens; 90th percentile ~210 tokens when long context included; average response tokens ~60. We've included a token histogram in lumos_token_profile.csv.
- Success criteria (initial): p95 latency < 300ms for generation (we'd prefer <300ms if possible), error rate <0.5% over trial window, and rerank precision@1 >= 0.88 on sampled queries. Cost not to exceed $X/day for the trial — procurement will confirm exact thresholds and come back with PO timeline.

Amit will upload the files to the shared Drive by EOD. No regulated PII in the samples — all customer identifiers are hashed. We do use prefix caching in our client partly (session affinity for active threads) which means you'll likely see repeated prefixes for active users.

Priya Sharma
Director of Product, Lumos Analytics
Attachments: lumos_token_profile.csv, lumos_sample_requests.json
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-30T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Lumos trial: workload intake + success criteria checklist

Looping in technical notes / what I need from Priya/Amit during calibration: 

- Exact RPS spike schedule (if you have campaign calendar windows) or synthetic trigger events we can replay. If not available, we'll emulate 3 burst windows/day at the stated magnitude.
- Concurrency definition: do you count a session as open across multiple requests (long lived) or per-request concurrency? This matters for connection pooling and KV cache warmups.
- For reranking, confirm whether you expect re-ranking to run as an inline step in the same request path or as a separate batch job that feeds results back (impacts p95 chain latency).

Benchmarking plan (high level):
1) Ingest their sample file and compute token-length distributions; build a synthetic generator that reproduces real-world histograms.
2) Run a 10-minute smoke at 50% baseline to verify correctness and latency.
3) Run burst windows + steady-state runs to measure p50/p95/p99.
4) Produce a short readout with recommended instance type, batching settings, and expected unit costs.

I'll own steps 1–3. Soojin, can you prepare the evaluation rubric template (we should include both quantitative gates and a few manual QA prompts for hallucination checks)?

Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Priya Sharma <priya@lumosanalytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, procurement@lumosanalytics.com
Date: 2027-03-31T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Lumos trial: workload intake + success criteria checklist

Perfect — thanks Priya and Amit for the uploads. Quick confirmation and actions from here: 

- Redwood will validate the CSV/JSON and return a short token-distribution report by Fri 2027-04-02. (Ben owns.)
- We'll schedule a 30-minute calibration call on Mon 2027-04-05 to lock the MAP and finalize PO timelines. I've sent a calendar invite separately.
- Soojin will share the evaluation rubric template by Mon 2027-04-05 so Lumos can add any product-specific checks.

If procurement needs anything from our side for an expedited PO, let me know and I’ll loop in Finance. Looking forward to kicking this off.

Best,
Marissa
Mid-Market AE | Redwood Inference
Attachment stubs: mutual-action-plan-v1.pdf
